newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SIX INNINGS OF NO-HIT BALL NOT ENOUGH FOR WOEFUL CUBS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SIX INNINGS OF NO-HIT BALL NOT ENOUGH FOR WOEFUL CUBS.

text.p: Chicago got six innings of no-hit pitching from starter Steve Trachsel but it was not enough for the woeful Cubs, who lost 4-3 to the Pittsburgh Pirates on Thursday to remain winless at home.

Jason Kendall doubled home the tying run with two out in the ninth and scored the eventual winning run on shortstop Rey Sanchez's throwing error as the Pirates rallied for a pair of runs against closer Mel Rojas (0-1).

Overshadowed in the loss was an outstanding performance by Trachsel, who did not allow a hit until Mark Johnson's leadoff double in the seventh. Trachsel allowed two runs -- one earned -- and three hits over seven innings, walking one and striking out five.
Kendall caught a break in his at-bat when he appeared to go around on a Rojas fastball on the outside corner that would have been strike three, but home plate umpire Bruce Froeming called it a ball.
After Kendall's second-chance double, Jose Guillen followed with a slow grounder to Sanchez, whose throw was in the dirt, allowing Kendall to score.

"I was concerned that I had struck out on the pitch Rojas had thrown before the double," Kendall said. "Obviously, the umpire didn't see me swing and I feel good about that. I was able to get a second chance and I hit a good pitch from Rojas and turned the game around."
The Pirates got a run without benefit of a hit in the first.

Jermaine Allensworth struck out but reached on a wild pitch. He stole second and moved to third on Trachsel's error. One out later he scored when Al Martin was picked off first but stayed in the rundown long enough for Allensworth to cross the plate.

Chicago (2-17) tied it in the second but Pittsburgh went ahead 2-1 in the seventh. Johnson led off with a double for the Bucs' first hit, moved to third on Kevin Elster's single and scored on Kendall's sacrifice fly.
The Cubs scored twice in their half of the seventh for a 3-2 lead before the winning ninth-inning rally by the Pirates.
Rich Loiselle (1-0) notched the victory by tossing two scoreless innings in relief.
"I don't feel sorry for the Cubs, they are in our division," Pirates manager Gene Lamont said. "I'm sure it is tough for them but we have to worry about our club."
